antidotes.why: Balance in food, rest, work and sleep is the yoga that ends sorrow.
Even the enemy is sent to rest.
Work done with huge strain for ego or pleasure is rajasic.
I still have to do this burns; do what comes and live at ease.

chains.summary: Wherever there is craving, the round of the world is there. The list of things done and not done has never ended for anyone. Everyone suffers from straining, and no one sees it.
chains.title: Where craving is, the round is

verses.m: Everyone is miserable from straining after things, and no one realises it. By this single teaching the fortunate one finds peace.
verses.sa: आयासात्सकलो दुःखी नैनं जानाति कश्चन । अनेनैवोपदेशेन धन्यः प्राप्नोति निर्वृतिम् ॥

depicts.m: Enough of wealth, of desire, even of good deeds. In this wilderness of life the mind never found rest in them.
depicts.sa: अलमर्थेन कामेन सुकृतेनापि कर्मणा । एभ्यः संसारकान्तारे न विश्रान्तमभून् मनः ॥
depicts.why: Depicts a mind that has run through the wilderness and is tired.

depicts.m: For one whose heart is scorched by the blazing sun of 'things I must do', where is happiness without the cooling rain of calm?
depicts.why: Names the burning weight of I still have to do this.

depicts.m: Keep quiet and you are dumb; speak well and you are a babbler or a windbag; stay close and you are pushy; keep away and you lack confidence; be patient and you are a coward; refuse to put up with things and you are ill-bred. The duty of serving another is deep indeed, beyond the reach even of yogis.
depicts.sa: मौनान्मूकः प्रवचनपटुर्वातुलो जल्पको वा धृष्टः पार्श्वे वसति च सदा दूरतश्चाप्रगल्भः । क्षान्त्या भीरुर्यदि न सहते प्रायशो नाभिजातः सेवाधर्मः परमगहनो योगिनामप्यगम्यः ॥
depicts.why: Shows exhaustion at never getting it right for a superior.

depicts.m: O heart, why do you enter into weariness, day after day trying to please the minds of others in so many ways, to win their favour? When you are at peace within, your own clear resolve rises by itself like a cluster of wish-granting gems: what wish of yours would it not fulfil?
depicts.sa: परेषां चेतांसि प्रतिदिवसमाराध्य बहुधा प्रसादं किं नेतुं विशसि हृदय क्लेशकलितम् । प्रसन्ने त्वय्यन्तः स्वयमुदितचिन्तामणिगणो विविक्तः संकल्पः किमभिलषितं पुष्यति न ते ॥
depicts.why: Gives daily effort to win other people's favour.

depicts.m: I am like the mother of two gamblers playing against each other, great sage. I cannot wish one victory without wishing the other defeat.
depicts.sa: सोऽहं कित्नवमातेव द्वयोरपि महामुने / नैकस्य जयमाशंसे द्वितीयस्य पराजयम्
depicts.why: Speaks as one worn down by kinsmen's quarrels.

depicts.sa: Be at rest, be free, and work.
depicts.why: They come home and think of the work for the next day.

depicts.r: Complete Works, Vol. 6, Notes of Class Talks and Lectures: On Bhakti-Yoga, p. 91
depicts.sa: Lord! I have become weary. Oh, take me by the hand, Lord, I take shelter with Thee

depicts.m: Carried along on endless great waves of tasks, the mind never gets a moment's rest; its depths dance with worry. 'This I've done, this I'm doing, this I'll do': so the bird of the mind, tangled in a net of reckonings, faints.
depicts.sa: उह्यमानमनन्तेषु चेतः कार्यमहोर्मिषु । क्षणमेति न विश्रान्तिं चिन्ताताण्डविताशयम् ॥ इदं कृतं करोमीदं करिष्यामीदमित्यलम् । कलनाजालवलिता मूर्च्छिता मतिपक्षिणी ॥
depicts.why: Shows a mind that never gets a moment's rest.

gloss: Śrama is being worn out by ceaseless doing. Ashtavakra: everyone suffers from straining (āyāsa) and no one notices. Prahlada says he was worn out by decisions and duties.

heals.m: For one whose heart is scorched by the blazing sun of 'things I must do', where is happiness without the cooling rain of calm?
Your right is to the work alone, never to its fruits. Do not let the fruit be your motive, and do not cling to doing nothing.
heals.sa: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन । मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥

heals.m: Yoga is not for one who eats too much, nor for one who does not eat at all; not for one who sleeps too much, nor for one who keeps awake too long, Arjuna.
heals.sa: नात्यश्नतस्तु योगोऽस्ति न चैकान्तमनश्नतः । न चातिस्वप्नशीलस्य जाग्रतो नैव चार्जुन ॥
heals.why: Names the extremes of food and sleep as what blocks steadiness.

heals.m: For one who is moderate in food and recreation, measured in effort at work, moderate in sleep and waking, yoga becomes the destroyer of sorrow.
heals.sa: युक्ताहारविहारस्य युक्तचेष्टस्य कर्मसु । युक्तस्वप्नावबोधस्य योगो भवति दुःखहा ॥
heals.why: Gives measure in food rest work and sleep as relief.

heals.m: Staying turned inward while doing all the outer work that comes to you, you will never grow weary, and you will be free of the sense of being the doer.
heals.sa: अन्तर्मुखः सन्सततं समस्तं कुर्वन्बहिष्ठं खलु कार्यजातम् । न खेदमायासि कदाचिदेव निराकृताहंकृतितामुपैषि ॥
heals.why: Weariness is tied to the doer-sense, not to the work.

heals.m: Weighing what helps and what harms, and with hundreds of royal duties, I was utterly worn out, Lord. For a moment now, I have found rest.
heals.sa: हिताहितविचारेण राजकार्यशतेन च । अत्यहं श्रमितो देव क्षणं विश्रामतां गतः ॥

heals.m: The fool is restless even when doing nothing; the skilful one stays calm even when doing everything that needs doing.
heals.sa: अकुर्वन्नपि सङ्क्षोभाद् व्यग्रः सर्वत्र मूढधीः । कुर्वन्नपि तु कृत्यानि कुशलो हि निराकुलः ॥
heals.why: Shows busyness itself is not the cause.

heals.m: O heart, why do you enter into weariness, day after day trying to please the minds of others in so many ways, to win their favour? When you are at peace within, your own clear resolve rises by itself like a cluster of wish-granting gems: what wish of yours would it not fulfil?
heals.sa: परेषां चेतांसि प्रतिदिवसमाराध्य बहुधा प्रसादं किं नेतुं विशसि हृदय क्लेशकलितम् । प्रसन्ने त्वय्यन्तः स्वयमुदितचिन्तामणिगणो विविक्तः संकल्पः किमभिलषितं पुष्यति न ते ॥
heals.why: Shows the poet asking his own heart why it enters this weariness.

hero.m: Everyone is miserable from straining after things, and no one realises it. By this single teaching the fortunate one finds peace.
hero.sa: आयासात्सकलो दुःखी नैनं जानाति कश्चन । अनेनैवोपदेशेन धन्यः प्राप्नोति निर्वृतिम् ॥

loci.m: Everyone is miserable from straining after things, and no one realises it. By this single teaching the fortunate one finds peace.
loci.sa: आयासात्सकलो दुःखी नैनं जानाति कश्चन । अनेनैवोपदेशेन धन्यः प्राप्नोति निर्वृतिम् ॥

practices.m: Friend mind, what is the use of so much chatter? Friend mind, all this is mere speculation. I have told you the heart of it: you are reality itself, vast as the sky.
practices.sa: सखे मनः किं बहुजल्पितेन सखे मनः सर्वमिदं वितर्क्यम् । यत्सारभूतं कथितं मया ते त्वमेव तत्त्वं गगनोपमोऽसि ॥

practices.m: Wealth has three destinies: giving, enjoying and loss. Whoever neither gives nor enjoys it meets the third.
practices.sa: दानं भोगो नाशस्तिस्रो गतयो भवन्ति वित्तस्य । यो न ददाति न भुङ्क्ते तस्य तृतीया गतिर्भवति ॥

practices.m: Wish for what can be had, never for what cannot. Enjoy what is in front of you now, and do not grieve over what has not yet come.
practices.why: Shows enjoying what is present is named as the practice.

practices.m: No one in this world gains real wealth through greed. Enough of greed, my son. Be at peace.
practices.r: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
practices.sa: न लोभादर्थसंपत्तिर्नराणामिह दृश्यते / तदलं तात लोभेन प्रशाम्य भरतर्षभ ॥

practices.m: The seventh is to see the whole world as filled with me, and to regard good people as greater than me. The eighth is to be content with whatever comes, and never, even in a dream, to look for faults in others.
practices.sa: सातवँ सम मोहि मय जग देखा। मोतें संत अधिक करि लेखा॥ आठवँ जथालाभ संतोषा। सपनेहुँ नहिं देखइ परदोषा ॥
practices.why: Shows contentment named as a form of devotion.

practices.m: Will I ever live like this? By the grace of kind Raghunath, will I take on the nature of a saint: always content with what comes, wanting nothing from anyone, always devoted to others' good, keeping my vow in mind, deed and word; hearing very harsh words and not burning in that fire; free of pride, even and cool of mind, speaking of others' virtues and not their faults; letting go of the body's worries, bearing joy and sorrow with an even mind?
practices.sa: कबहुँक हौं यहि रहनि रहौंगो। श्रीरघुनाथ-कृपालु-कृपातें संत-सुभाव गहौंगो॥ ९॥ जथालाभसंतोष सदा, काहू सों कछु न चहांगो। पर-हित-निरत निरंतर, मन क्रम बचन नेम निबहौंगो॥ … परुष बचन अति दुसह श्रवन सुनि तेहि पावक न दहांगो। बिगत मान, सम सीतल मन, पर-गुन नहिं दोष कहाँगो॥ ३॥ परिहरि देह-जनित चिंता, दुख-सुख समबुद्धि सहोंगो।

practices.m: In a vessel full of awakening, filled with the oil of detachment and fitted with the wick of devotion, behold the lamp of knowing. In the hollow darkness of delusion it rises of itself. Make detachment the lower fire-stick and knowledge the upper.
practices.sa: स होवाच । वैराग्यतैलसम्पूर्णे भक्तिवर्तिसमन्विते । प्रबोधपूर्णपात्रे तु ज्ञप्तिदीपं विलोकयेत् ॥ मोहान्धकारे निःसारे उदेति स्वयमेव हि । वैराग्यमरणिं कृत्वा ज्ञानं कृत्वोत्तरारणिम् ॥
practices.why: Shows the light then rises of itself.

practices.m: Four gatekeepers are named at the door of freedom: calm, inquiry, contentment, and the company of good people. Take refuge in even one of them with full effort, setting all else aside; when one is won, all four come under your control.
practices.sa: मोक्षद्वारे द्वारपालश्चत्वारः परिकीर्तिताः । शमो विचारः सन्तोषश्चतुर्थः साधुसङ्गमः ॥ एकं वा सर्वयत्नेन सर्वमुत्सृज्य संश्रयेत् । एकस्मिन्वशगे यान्ति चत्वारोऽपि वशं गताः ॥
practices.why: Contentment is named as a door, not a reward.

stories.l: In family feuds, the weapon that works is gentleness, patience and respect.
stories.s: Even Krishna struggles with his clan: he does their work, bears their harsh words, and feels like the mother of two gamblers playing each other. Narada tells him the only weapon that works is soft: generosity, patience, sincerity, gentleness and respect.
stories.t: Krishna's family troubles: the weapon not made of iron

stories.l: When everything you knew is underwater, you have not been forgotten; you are being held.
stories.s: At the end of an age, the sage Markandeya drifts alone over a flooded world and sees a radiant child on a banyan branch. The child draws him inside his body, where he sees all the worlds, then asks if he has been resting, tired. Narayana explains he showed himself because he saw Markandeya's distress. Markandeya tells the Pandavas that this child is Krishna, sitting with them.
stories.t: Markandeya and the child on the banyan leaf

stories.l: Faithful waiting is rewarded; return what was entrusted to you, and more.
stories.s: Hanuman finds Bharata thin, in bark clothes, still waiting. Hearing Ram is near, Bharata faints with joy: a person who stays alive will find joy, even after a hundred years. He places the sandals back on Ram's feet and hands back the kingdom he kept in trust, now ten times richer.

stories.l: Fight with everything you have; when your strength runs out, call. Help comes running.
stories.s: An elephant king is seized by a crocodile in a lake and struggles for a thousand years with all his strength and his herd. Only when his strength is gone does he call out to Hari, who leaves his mount behind and runs barefoot to free him. Surdas returns to the story again and again (vp.11, 21, 241, 256).
stories.t: The elephant who finally called (as Surdas sings it)
